**STEP 1 - Scene:** A chicken wrap (flour tortilla rolled around shredded lettuce, carrot, and chicken), cut in half and served on a white paper plate. A glass of cola sits on the tray beside the plate; I've excluded it as a separate drink.

**STEP 2 - Vessel:** White paper plate, about 20 cm diameter. Area = 3.14 × 10² ≈ 314 cm².

**STEP 3 - Items:** (1) flour tortilla wrap, two halves; (2) shredded chicken; (3) shredded lettuce; (4) carrot strips; (5) light creamy sauce, visible as a pale sheen inside.

**STEP 4 - Area:** The two wrap halves together cover about 104 cm², roughly 33% of the plate. Tortilla ~19%, lettuce ~8%, chicken ~4%, carrot ~2%. Sauce is hidden inside the wrap, so I count it within the filling.

**STEP 5 - Volume:** Wrap envelope ≈ 104 cm² × 4 cm ≈ 416 ml gross.

**STEP 6 - Grams:** Tortilla is rolled and partly hollow, so an effective density of about 0.6 g/ml gives roughly 70 g (the shell plus its share of filling is accounted for below). Chicken ~25 g, lettuce ~35 g (loose leafy greens, low density), carrot ~10 g, sauce ~8 g. Total ≈ 148 g.

**STEP 7 - Energy:** Tortilla 70 g × 300 kcal/100 g = 210 kcal. Chicken 25 g × 165 = 41 kcal. Lettuce 35 g × 15 = 5 kcal. Carrot 10 g × 40 = 4 kcal. Sauce 8 g × 150 = 12 kcal. Total ≈ 272 kcal.

**STEP 8 - Sanity check:** Two wrap halves with a modest filling, about 150 g and roughly 270 kcal, is plausible for what is visible. The estimate is not inflated by a typical full serving.
